lemonade: Use when designing, building, redesigning or reviewing public-facing websites, Korean content portals, cultural venues, portfolios, marketing pages or a page from visual references. Also use when a frontend needs stronger composition, readable hierarchy, faithful reference interpretation or less generic design. For app screens, preserve the existing workflow and use only relevant composition guidance.
lemonade-brandkit: Use when creating visual identity boards, logo concepts, brand guidelines, or brand application images.
lemonade-brutalist: Use when explicitly requesting an industrial, brutalist, Swiss-grid or terminal-inspired visual style, or continuing an established design in that language. Dense schedules or data alone do not trigger this aesthetic.
lemonade-gpt: Use when explicitly requesting the expressive frontend and motion preset, or continuing a frontend that already uses its visual language. Keep the existing stack, references, brand and functional information; GSAP and dramatic layouts are optional techniques.
lemonade-image-to-code: Use when implementing a supplied screenshot, image or selected mockup as a faithful responsive frontend, or when an explicitly requested image-first design workflow must be turned into code.
lemonade-imagegen-mobile: Use when generating mobile app screen concepts or visual flows for iOS, Android or cross-platform products. This mode produces visual references; implementation belongs to a separate request.
lemonade-imagegen-web: Use when generating website or individual section reference images, visual directions or website mockups. This mode produces images; use lemonade-image-to-code for implementation.
lemonade-minimalist: Use when explicitly requesting a restrained utilitarian or editorial minimalist style, or continuing an established minimalist design. Preserve existing brand colors, content density required by the task and useful operational navigation.
lemonade-output: Use when a user requires complete implementation output without omitted functions, truncated code or unfinished scaffolding. Honest labels for missing user assets, example data and unconnected services must remain visible.
lemonade-redesign: Use when improving an existing implemented website or interface while preserving its actual content, brand and working behavior. A new page that only has brand colors is not automatically a redesign task.
lemonade-soft: Use when explicitly requesting a soft, tactile visual style with layered surfaces and subtle motion, or continuing a design already using that style. Do not replace an established brand or task-driven information structure merely to add agency-style effects.
lemonade-stitch: Use when deriving a semantic DESIGN.md specification from existing screens for a Google Stitch workflow, or when explicitly requesting that design-system format. Use only tools actually available and preserve supplied brand and functional constraints.
lemonade-v1: Use when explicitly requesting the classic frontend design preset or continuing a project established with that preset. Use lemonade for normal reference-led website work. Shared brand, content and accessibility priorities still apply.
lemonade-v2-experimental: Use when explicitly requesting the experimental variance, motion and density presets, or when continuing a project that already uses them. Use lemonade for the normal reference-led workflow.
